transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm doing this right, I've never really been to a doctor for something like this before. 

I guess what pushed me to make this appointment is... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, because I really do try to be good at my job. I'm an auditor, and I pride myself on being responsible. But lately, I keep starting these follow-up items after my audits, or after mentorship events, and I have every intention of finishing them right then. I really do. But then... I don't know, I'll find out days later that the final email, or a review note, or a form never actually got done. 

It's probably just a silly little thing, and I'm usually so on top of my work, but I just don't want anyone to think I'm careless, you know? Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing I should be telling you?

When you think back to those unfinished follow-up items, what usually gets in the way—do you find yourself getting distracted by other things and simply forgetting, or is it more that you start worrying or overthinking the task and put it off?

Oh, um, I wouldn't say it's worrying. I really do try to be confident in my work, so I don't want to give the impression that I can't handle the pressure or anything like that. I think it's more... well, getting distracted, maybe? Just a little bit. 

Like, if I'm trying to review an audit file, I really am trying to focus on it. But then a Slack ping will pop up, or... or I'll hear someone talking outside my office. Or sometimes it's not even anything happening around me, I'll just suddenly have a thought about my marathon training, and... I don't know, it just pulls me completely off track. 

I always mean to go right back to the file, I promise I do. It's just that my attention sort of... shifts without me realizing it? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible employee. I really do work hard, and I care about doing a good job. Does that answer your question okay?
Thinking back to your school years, did you notice similar patterns of getting easily distracted or losing focus on tasks, even before you started your career as an auditor?

Oh, um... yes, I suppose so. I mean, I really was a good student overall, I promise! I always wanted my teachers to be happy with me. But... well, if I'm being completely honest, even back in elementary school, my report cards usually had a little note saying that I was a bright girl, but... maybe I rushed past small details, or lost my assignments sometimes. And, um, occasionally they'd say I talked out of turn or needed a few extra reminders to finish my work. 

I really wasn't trying to be disruptive or anything, I just got so eager to participate, I think. My mother actually still jokes about it today. She always says I was the kind of kid who could easily ace a test, but then completely forget to turn in the big project that was sitting right there in my backpack. 

It's just a silly family joke now, but... does that make sense? Is that the kind of background information you were looking for?
Aside from work, do you notice similar difficulties with distraction, disorganization, or forgetfulness affecting your daily life at home or in your personal relationships?

Oh, um... yes, I suppose it does happen at home, too. I really try to be a good partner, I promise I do, but... well, if I'm being completely honest, my husband has actually had to take over paying the bills and managing some of the commitments I originally agreed to handle. He's so patient with me, but I think it's just because he realized he can't always count on me to complete them reliably. I feel so awful saying that out loud. I hope you don't think I'm a terrible wife! I really do try.

And, actually... since we're talking about how much this is affecting things... I probably should have been a little more upfront earlier about work. I was just a little too embarrassed to admit it right away. But those unfinished follow-ups I mentioned? It actually reached the point recently where a client review was affected by my mistakes. I'm just so worried that people are starting to question whether I can handle the promotion I've been working so hard toward. 

I really want them to trust me, and I want to do a good job. Is it okay that I'm sharing all of this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.

Do you often feel restless or fidgety, have trouble sitting still for long periods, or find yourself talking excessively or acting impulsively, like interrupting others or making quick decisions without thinking them through?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I'm completely unable to sit still. I really do try my best to be professional, especially during meetings. I know how important it is to look attentive. But... I guess, if I'm being honest, I might be a little bit fidgety sometimes? 

Like, when I'm sitting in those long audit reviews, I usually find myself tapping my foot under the table, or... or maybe clicking my pen a few times. I try to keep it quiet! But I do end up shifting around in my chair quite a bit. One of my colleagues actually joked the other day that she can always hear my leg going under the desk. 

I really hope it's not too distracting for anyone else. I'm just trying to stay alert, you know? I don't want to come across like I'm not taking the meeting seriously, because I really do care. Does that... is that the kind of restlessness you mean? I hope I'm answering this right.

Do you often find yourself interrupting others in conversation, finishing their sentences, or making quick decisions—like agreeing to a commitment or purchase—without fully thinking them through first?

Oh, um... well, I always try my hardest to be a good listener. I really believe it's important to let people speak and feel heard, especially at work. But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest again... 

Sometimes, especially when I'm working with the junior auditors on my team, I do catch myself jumping into conversations before they've actually finished their sentences. It's really not because I want to be rude or talk over them! I promise. It's just that... well, the answer or the idea pops up, and it feels so urgent in my head that I just sort of blurt it out before I can even stop myself. 

I always try to apologize right away when I realize I've done it. I really hate the idea of making anyone feel like I don't value their input, and I hope they know I mean well. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible manager... Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm answering correctly.

Thinking back to before you turned 12 years old, do you remember your fidgeting, impulsive blurting out, or losing track of assignments being noticeable enough that teachers or your parents specifically commented on it at that age?

Oh, goodness... well, I was always a very happy kid, and I really did love school. I wanted my teachers to be proud of me, I really did. But... yes, I suppose if you looked back at my elementary school report cards, there were definitely some comments. 

They always made sure to say I was a bright student, which was so sweet of them! But then... they would usually add that I tended to rush past the small details, or that I talked out of turn sometimes. And, um, I guess I did lose my assignments pretty often, too. The teachers mentioned I needed a lot of reminders just to finish my work. I never meant to be a disruption, I just... I don't know, I just lost track of things so easily. 

Actually, my mother still jokes about it to this day. She always tells people that I was the kind of kid who could completely ace a test, but then totally forget to turn in the big project that was sitting right there in my backpack. I always felt so terrible when I disappointed them. 

Does that... does that help answer your question? I hope that's the kind of background information you were looking for. I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
